claims.text: PostgreSQL automatically creates a unique index (one that rejects duplicate values) when a PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint (no two rows share a value) is declared, to enforce it.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 11.6 Unique Indexes; 5.5.3 Unique Constraints; 5.5.4 Primary Keys

claims.text: Declaring a foreign key (REFERENCES) does not create an index on the referencing columns; since it is not always needed, that is left to the user. An index adds overhead to writes on its table.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 5.5.5 Foreign Keys (last paragraph); 11.1 Indexes Introduction (indexes add overhead); EF Core docs Relationships > Conventions ('Indexes have overhead')

claims.text: By convention EF Core creates an index for the property or properties of each foreign key in its model (ForeignKeyIndexConvention), and a migration generated after the model change contains the matching CreateIndex.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Modeling > Relationships > Conventions, 'Indexes'; Modeling > Indexes ('By convention, an index is created in each property ... used as a foreign key')

claims.text: EF Core does not create the foreign key index when the foreign key's properties are already covered by an existing index or primary key (one that starts with those properties).
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Modeling > Relationships > Conventions, 'Indexes' NOTE ('EF does not create indexes for properties that are already covered by an existing index or primary key constraint')

claims.text: EF Core discovers relationships from navigations (properties holding a related entity) or explicit HasOne/HasMany; an int OrderId on an entity with no navigation and no relationship configuration is a plain property, not a foreign key.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Modeling > Relationships > Conventions ('Discovering relationships' from navigations); examples/don-hang @ stage-1 DonHangDbContextModelSnapshot.cs (no relationship for Payment)

claims.text: At stage-1, db/schema.sql declares orders.customer_id, order_items.order_id, order_items.product_id and payments.order_id with REFERENCES, order_items has PRIMARY KEY (order_id, product_id), customers.email is UNIQUE, and the file contains no CREATE INDEX.

AddOrderCustomerNavigation.Up runs CreateIndex IX_orders_customer_id on orders(customer_id); DonHangDbContext maps HasOne(o => o.Customer).WithMany().HasForeignKey(o => o.CustomerId). So at stage-1 the index on orders.customer_id comes from this migration.
At stage-1 the only HasIndex in DonHangDbContext is e.HasIndex(c => c.Email).IsUnique() on Customer.
EF Core's default index name is IX_<table>_<column(s)>, as in IX_orders_customer_id and IX_customers_email.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Modeling > Indexes ('Index name': 'By convention, indexes created in a relational database are named IX_<type name>_<property name>'); migrations at stage-1

claims.text: InitialCreate creates order_items with PK (order_id, product_id) and FK_order_items_orders_order_id, no CreateIndex for order_items (only IX_customers_email); MigrationBaseline marks InitialCreate applied without running it on the lab db.
Payment has an OrderId property but no navigation, and DonHangDbContext configures no relationship for Payment, so no migration creates a foreign key or an index for payments.order_id.

Try it: pg_indexes (a system view, one row per index) for order_items and payments lists exactly order_items_pkey (UNIQUE btree (order_id, product_id)) and payments_pkey (UNIQUE btree (id)) at stage-1 and stage-2.
claims.source_hint: live run on the lab db 2026-09-28 (same at stage-1 and stage-2; also verified on a scratch db built from stage-1 db/schema.sql); PostgreSQL 17 docs: 52.x pg_indexes view

claims.text: An index on the referencing columns lets PostgreSQL find the rows that point at one parent row without reading the whole table.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 5.5.5 Foreign Keys (index on referencing columns); 11.1 Indexes Introduction

claims.text: A multicolumn B-tree index is ordered by its first column first, so it can be used to find rows by a condition on that leading column alone.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 11.3 Multicolumn Indexes ('most efficient when there are constraints on the leading (leftmost) columns')
